target_customer: Cloud architects, DevOps and platform engineering teams using Terraform or OpenTofu
problem: Engineers find infrastructure as code hard to learn and to keep consistent across teams; architecture diagrams drift from deployed reality.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user with a free tier; paid plans cited at 25 euros to $99 per user per month by third parties
product_category: Visual cloud infrastructure design and management platform

founders.name: Chafik Belhaoues
founders.background_notes: YC page: 17 years in infrastructure, from SRE and cloud architect to developer.

founders.name: Jeremy Albinet
founders.background_notes: YC page: 10 years designing cloud architectures.

competitors.name: Cloudcraft
competitors.what: Cloud architecture diagrams generated from AWS accounts, with Terraform export at the time
competitors.traction_then: Existed before the batch; source is the November 2022 Datadog acquisition announcement, about ten months after the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Bidirectional visual design and Terraform code generation across multiple clouds, state and drift handling, for a team of two to nine.

defensibility.rationale: Teams store architectures, modules and workflows in the tool, but Terraform vendors and diagram tools could add similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Datadog bought Cloudcraft in November 2022 and later dropped its Terraform export; no incumbent acquired Brainboard as of the sources.

market_need_then: Terraform adoption was growing and the YC page frames a learning curve problem for moving to infrastructure as code.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and promotional: 'The cloud is your canvas.'

branding.brand_signature: The cloud is your canvas tagline
branding.community_and_virality: Active blog and Terraform community content; no merch or fan evidence

brand_strength.rationale: Clear visual metaphor but generic name shared with other whiteboard products and no third party press about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Brainboard, started by two former Scaleway engineers, joined YC in Winter 2022 and is still active with AWS and Azure marketplace listings and blue chip logos on its site. Aggregators show only pre-seed and seed sized funding of roughly $1.7M to $2.6M, and a directory claims $1.5M 2024 revenue, which is unverified. It looks like a durable but small business so far.
notes: Funding figures conflict: $1.05M seed July 2021, $1.2M pre-seed November 2021, $2.1M seed II April 2022 (CB Insights); totals $1.7M to $2.6M. All from aggregators, so no round is recorded. The company site says it is backed by Y Combinator, Moonfire, Kima Ventures and Evolem. Cloudcraft is dated after the batch and noted as such. Location conflicts (New York per YC, Paris per directories). Founder education not found. Completeness pass: only the Nov 2021 $1.2M pre-seed is recorded, which Seedtable and CB Insights agree on; it rests on databases only. The July 2021 $1.05M, Jan 2022 $500K and April 2022 $2.1M figures conflict across databases and stay unrecorded. A Seedtable total of $1.7M and a CB Insights total of $2.6M are noted as a known gap.
